findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/NumberTheory/ADEInequality.lean:154 `theorem lt_three {p q r : ℕ+} (hpq : p ≤ q) (hqr : q ≤ r) (H : 1 < sumInv {p, q, r}) : p < 3`; :166 `lt_four`; :176 `lt_six`; :109 `sumInv_pqr`. No file under TauCeti/ mentions `ADEInequality` (grep for `ADEInequality|sumInv` returns no hits in TauCeti/).
findings.fix: Delete `three_arm_arith` together with the denominator-clearing scaffolding `hpa`/`hpb`/`hpc`/`hclear`/`hnat` at lines 461-471, `public import Mathlib.NumberTheory.ADEInequality`, and in `arms_of_isFiniteType_star_three` set `p : ℕ+ := ⟨a+1, a.succ_pos⟩` (likewise `q`, `r`), turn `hbound` into `1 < ADEInequality.sumInv {p,q,r}` by `ADEInequality.sumInv_pqr` (`hbound` is already in the `(·)⁻¹` form the Mathlib lemmas want, so no `field_simp` is needed), then `lt_three` gives `a ≤ 1`, `lt_four` gives `b ≤ 2` in the `a = 1` branch, and `lt_six` gives `c ≤ 4` in the `b = 2` branch.
findings.issue: `three_arm_arith` re-proves Mathlib's ADE inequality classification. Mathlib's `ADEInequality.lt_three (hpq : p ≤ q) (hqr : q ≤ r) (H : 1 < sumInv {p,q,r}) : p < 3`, `ADEInequality.lt_four (hqr : q ≤ r) (H : 1 < sumInv {2,q,r}) : q < 4` and `ADEInequality.lt_six (H : 1 < sumInv {2,3,r}) : r < 6` are exactly the three case-splitting steps of this private lemma, in the same `p ≤ q ≤ r` ordered form (`ADEInequality.admissible_of_one_lt_sumInv_aux'` chains them into the full classification).

findings.fix: Reuse Mathlib's matrix: either read the arm entries off `CartanMatrix.A` (with the `Fin` coercions the star already has via `Fin (ℓ i)`), or, if the ℕ-indexed helper is kept for the unbounded positions, record and use the identity `chainEntry (i : Fin n) (j : Fin n) = CartanMatrix.A n i j` (provable by `simp [chainEntry, CartanMatrix.A]; grind`, the shape used at Classical.lean:171) so the two chain descriptions cannot drift.
findings.issue: `chainEntry s t = if s = t then 2 else if s = t + 1 then -1 else if t = s + 1 then -1 else 0` is Mathlib's `CartanMatrix.A` entry rule transcribed to ℕ indices: `CartanMatrix.A n i j = if i = j then 2 else if i.val + 1 = j.val ∨ j.val + 1 = i.val then -1 else 0`. This repo already treats `CartanMatrix.A` as the canonical chain (`isFiniteType_cartanMatrix_A`, `DynkinType.cartanMatrix_A`), so the star now carries a second, unconnected description of the same simply-laced chain, and nothing ties the one-armed star to type `A`.

findings.fix: Delete it; a call site excluding a diagram writes `card_sub_two_lt_sum_inv_of_isFiniteType_star (heq ▸ h.submatrix he)` directly, which is the idiom `IsFiniteType.submatrix` was documented for in Basic.lean.
findings.issue: `card_sub_two_lt_sum_inv_of_star_submatrix` is a thin wrapper: its whole proof is `card_sub_two_lt_sum_inv_of_isFiniteType_star (heq ▸ h.submatrix he)`, composing two public declarations, and it has no consumer anywhere in the repository.

summary: The star construction and the subdominant-vector elimination tool are genuinely new, but the three-armed arithmetic re-derives Mathlib's `ADEInequality` (`lt_three`/`lt_four`/`lt_six`) verbatim, and `chainEntry` restates the entry rule of `CartanMatrix.A`, which this repo already uses as its canonical chain matrix.
